page: Google Cloud Platform n2-highcpu-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance belonging to the N2 family. It features 8 vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores of an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz, utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The instance is configured with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 1.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include bundled local storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 7430.34 and a PassMark CPU score of 8305.34. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 1138.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1409.67. Memory bandwidth remains in the average tier, reaching 412.9 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 48.32 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. The CPU supports AVX-512 vector extensions, which aids in workloads like software compilation and text processing, both of which registered average performance tiers.

The primary tradeoff of the n2-highcpu-8 is its low memory-to-vCPU ratio, which limits its utility for memory-intensive databases or large-scale data processing. However, this resource profile offers qualitative cost efficiency for compute-bound tasks that do not require large memory footprints, avoiding the expense of unutilized RAM. This instance is best suited for workloads such as static web serving, software compilation, lightweight text processing, and basic machine learning inference using small models.
